author_or_org: Per Aspera (Mark Scianna and Ryan Duffy)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source defines a forward deployed engineer as someone stationed at the customer site to bridge the gap between product capabilities and customer needs.
claims.quote: McGrew defines a forward deployed engineer as someone “who sits at the customer site and fills the gap between what the product does and what the customer needs.”

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Palantir's model uses Echo teams of domain insiders to find high-leverage customer problems and Delta teams of rapid-prototyping engineers to ship a scrappy initial version in weeks rather than quarters.
claims.quote: Echo teams are domain insiders with a rebellious streak, embedded with customers to unearth real, high-leverage problems and manage relationships; Delta teams are rapid-prototyping engineers who build and deploy fast, working hand-in-hand with Echo to ship the scrappy v0 in weeks, not quarters.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source states that forward-deployed headcount sits in COGS and compresses gross margin while discovery work is heavy.
claims.quote: A forward function lives in COGS (even if it’s actually R&D) and compresses gross margin while discovery is heavy.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source says a healthy FDE loop raises revenue per FDE as software replaces engineers bridging the product-customer gap.
claims.quote: If it’s working, in a healthy loop, revenue per FDE will rise as software replaces the engineers who are bridging the gap between what the product can do and what the customer needs.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source says most organizations cannot stomach FDE because they want routine check-ins, approvals for technical choices, predictable roadmaps, and tight budget controls.
claims.quote: Most organizations simply can’t stomach this model. The average corporation, organization, or bureaucracy wants routine check-ins, approvals for every technical choice, predictable roadmaps, and tight budget controls. FDE affords no such creature comforts.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The source recommends working quickly—within 10 days—toward a live demo using real data as a specification.
claims.quote: **Demo as spec:** Work quickly (≤10 days) towards a live demo that relies on real data and creates _desire_ for your user(s).
